Why Fechin?

A Russian-American painter whose portraits feel alive: sharp faces, and wild brushwork all around them.

Trained by

Ilya Repin, Russia's great realist

Known for

Portraits that seem to look back at you

Signature

Precise faces, free and fearless paint

His belief

Recognize the work by its painting, not by the signature

Chapter I · 1881 — 1910

Russia: roots and training

1881Born, Kazan1895Art school1901Academy1909Graduates
  • Woodcarver's son, drawing altar designs by age 11
  • Studied under Repin in St. Petersburg
  • Bearing Away the Bride (1908) wins a top prize
  • 1910: Munich gold medal, first US show
Bearing Away the Bride, 1908

Chapter II · 1910 — 1927

Revolution and a new world

1917Revolution1923New York1927Taos
  • Taught in Kazan for a decade
  • Lost his parents; survived the 1921 famine
  • Arrived in New York at 42, quickly in demand
  • Tuberculosis sent him to Taos, New Mexico

Chapter III · 1927 — 1976

Taos, California and home

1933California1955Dies1976Kazan
  • Hand-carved his Taos house, now the Taos Art Museum
  • Moved to California; painted across Mexico and Asia
  • Died in Santa Monica, 1955
  • Reburied in Kazan, 1976

Technique 1

Selective finish

  • Eyes and face: carefully resolved
  • Clothes and background: loose strokes, scraped paint
  • Your eye goes straight to the person

Technique 2

A few strokes, a whole object

  • A handful of perfectly placed strokes
  • Your brain fills in the rest: "the beholder's share"
  • Not a photograph; he chooses what to show
Up close

Technique 3

Tools and surface

  • Palette knife for broad areas and movement
  • Thick paint beside thin, bare passages
  • Self-prepared canvases for a dry, broken texture
  • From life, rarely sketched first
